title: Solving simple trigonometric equations

match.reason: The new point is about solving trigonometric equations over 0° to 360° using the unit circle's symmetry, and the closest bank point teaches the same skill but its questions and depth are general, so it is unclear it matches this Year 10 Level 10A point closely enough to reuse or adapt.

draft.title: Solving simple trigonometric equations
card: To solve \(\sin x = 0.5\), use the calculator's inverse sine: \(\sin^{-1}(0.5) = 30^{\circ}\). This is the first solution.

On the unit circle, sine is the y-coordinate. Two angles from \(0^{\circ}\) to \(360^{\circ}\) have the same height, \(30^{\circ}\) and \(180^{\circ} - 30^{\circ} = 150^{\circ}\). So \(x = 30^{\circ}\) or \(150^{\circ}\).

Cosine is the x-coordinate, so its second angle is the mirror image across the x-axis: \(360^{\circ}\) minus the first. For \(\cos x = 0.8\), the calculator gives \(36.9^{\circ}\), so \(x = 36.9^{\circ}\) or \(323.1^{\circ}\).
draft.remember: Use the calculator for the first angle, then the unit circle for the second: 180° minus it for sine, 360° minus it for cosine.

a.q: Solve \(\sin x = 0.8\) for \(0^{\circ} \le x \le 360^{\circ}\). Give angles to 1 decimal place.
a.why: The calculator gives \(\sin^{-1}(0.8) \approx 53.1^{\circ}\). Sine is the y-coordinate, so the second angle is \(180^{\circ} - 53.1^{\circ} = 126.9^{\circ}\). Using \(360^{\circ} - 53.1^{\circ}\) is the rule for cosine, not sine.
a.clue: Sine is the height on the unit circle. Which other angle has the same height?

b.q: Leo solves \(\cos x = 0.5\) for \(0^{\circ} \le x \le 360^{\circ}\). Which pair of angles is correct?
b.why: The calculator gives \(\cos^{-1}(0.5) = 60^{\circ}\). Cosine is the x-coordinate, so the second angle is \(360^{\circ} - 60^{\circ} = 300^{\circ}\). The pair \(60^{\circ}\) and \(120^{\circ}\) uses the sine rule, \(180^{\circ}\) minus the first angle, which is wrong for cosine.
b.clue: Cosine is the x-coordinate. Mirror the angle across the x-axis.
